(p-544) In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah al-Layl (The Night).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the night when it covers﴾ ﴿and by the day when it appears in splendour﴾

Allah swears by the night and the day and their effect upon the universe, to show that they are two great signs.

The discussion of these two was already given in the surah before it, at His saying: ﴿By the day when it displays it, and by the night when it covers it﴾ [ash-Shams: 3–4].

The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, had already discussed these two verses at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾ [al-Isra': 12], in the surah of "Banu Isra'il", and mentioned all the texts on this meaning, as well as the effect of the night and the day on people's lives, the knowledge of reckoning (hisab, calculation of time), and the like.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 92, verse 3:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And by He Who created the male and the female﴾.

The Shaykh, may the mercy of Allah the Exalted be upon us and upon him, has already discussed this question and cited all the texts on it in several places. He pointed to all of them in Surah an-Najm, at the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And that He created the two pairs, the male and the female, from a drop of semen when it is emitted﴾ [an-Najm 53:45-46]. It has been recited in several readings (qira'at, the recognised variant readings of the Qur'an), among them ﴿khalaqa adh-dhakara wal-untha﴾ and among them "wadh-dhakara wal-untha."

Ibn Kathir cited it as traced back to the Prophet ﷺ in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, and in the well-known reading.

As for ﴿wa-ma khalaqa adh-dhakara wal-untha﴾, scholars differ over the word "ma" (ما). It is said that it is a verbal (masdariyyah) "ma," meaning: "and [by] the creating of the male and the female."

It is also said that it means "man" (من), meaning: "and by He Who created the male and the female."

On the first view, the oath is by one of Allah's attributes, which is the attribute of creation, and He singled out the male and the female because of the wondrous workmanship of Allah and the strength of His power, exalted be He, as will come.

On the reading "wadh-dhakara wal-untha," the oath is by a created thing, like the night and the day, because creation also contains the power of the Creator. And on the view that "ma" means "He who," the oath is by the Creator, exalted be He, and "ma" here is like its use in His saying: ﴿By the sky and He who built it﴾ [ash-Shams 91:5]. The most that can be said about it is its use (of "ma" for persons). Originally it is used for those who lack understanding, but in this case the sense of an attribute was taken into account, which is the attribute of creation, or in accordance with how the Arabs use it when there is a context. Like His saying: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:22], and His saying: ﴿So marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:3]. Because the sense of an attribute, which is enjoyment, was taken into account in it, the use of "ma" in place of "man" was permissible.

The singling out of the creation of the male and the female in this context draws attention to this attribute, because of the human inability to comprehend it, just as with the night and the day there is an inability on the part of humans to do anything specific regarding them, as we mentioned in the surah before it.

That is because the basic principle of masculinity and femininity is a matter beyond human perception and capabilities, and it is as follows:

First: In mammals, which are those possessing a womb that carries and gives birth, they reproduce through the union of males with females. The masculinity or femininity of the embryo is not something in which the two parents have any part. It is "from a drop of mixed fluid" (nutfah amshaj), meaning mixtures of the fluid of the father and the mother. He made this one a male and that one a female. It is thus a gift from Allah, as in His saying: ﴿He bestows female [offspring] on whom He wills, and bestows male [offspring] on whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed He is Knowing and Powerful﴾ [ash-Shura 42:49-50].

It has been established scientifically that the cause of masculinity and femininity lies on the side of the man. That is, the woman's fluid is suitable for both this and that, while the man's fluid is what makes the distinction, through a division that occurs in it. The woman is nothing more than a field (harth), and the man is the sower, and the type of crop comes about through him, as the noble verse indicates: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:223]. The field does not dispose of the crop; the disposal is through the one who tills.

This happens through a scientifically known principle, which is that the fertilising cell in the female is always and forever (p-546) composed of forty-eight units. It always and forever divides into two equal halves of twenty-four each. A part of it merges with the part of the male's cell, and the male's cell has forty-seven. The cell also always divides, at fertilisation, into two parts, but one of them has twenty-four and the other has twenty-three. So when Allah wills the embryo to be male, the part that has twenty-three precedes, and it merges with the counterpart of the female's cell, which has twenty-four, so that their total is forty-seven, and the child is male by Allah's permission.

And when Allah wills the embryo to be female, the part that has twenty-four from the man precedes, and it merges with the counterpart of the woman's cell, which has twenty-four, so their total is forty-eight, and the child is female by Allah's permission. It is the same in all animals.

As for plants, some trees have male and female distinguished, such as the date palm and the mulberry, for example. In the rest of the trees, a single tree bears both the male flower and the female flower, and the winds fertilise some of them from others.

Several people have told me of two strange cases regarding this:

The first: that there is a date palm still existing today which in some years produces a male (fahl) from which pollen is taken to pollinate the date palms, and in some years it produces a date palm that bears fruit.

Another person told me in the same session that among them there is a date palm tree, one half of which is a male from which pollen is taken to fertilise the palms, and the other half is a female palm which is fertilised from the other half because of its proximity.

A third also told me that his father cut down part of a male date palm because it was too numerous among the palms, and after it was cut, a date palm grew from its base, from its trunk and its roots, and it bears fruit. All of this is contrary to the usual custom, but it indicates the power of Allah the Exalted, and that He is the Creator of the male and the female.

As for the operation of this apparatus in animals, and even in tiny insects and their reproduction, it is beyond counting and limit.

They have mentioned, in the world of insects, one that fertilises itself by itself, by the rubbing of some of its thighs against others. All of this is something that no one knows or is able to bring into being except Allah, glory be to Him and exalted be He. If the rational person were to reflect on it, he would find in it, as we have mentioned, a dazzling power greater than what is in the night when it covers, and what is in the day when it appears, especially when the creature is small, like the gnat or what is smaller, which can barely be seen with the eye. Yet despite that, there is in it masculinity and femininity. Glory be to You, O Allah, how great is Your majesty.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 92, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾.

It has already been mentioned in the first surah His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies it, and he has certainly failed who corrupts it﴾ [al-Shams: 9-10]. Both are by striving toward it (Allah) and working for its sake. Here He says: "Indeed, your efforts," whatever they may be, "are diverse" (shatta), meaning: distant from one another, separated from each other.

Al-shatat (shatat) is distance and separation. Shatta is the plural of shatit, like marda (sick) being the plural of marid, and qatla (slain) of qatil, and the like. From it is the saying of the poet:

"Allah may bring together the scattered ones (al-shatitayn) after they had utterly assumed they would never meet."

This is the response (jawab) of the oath, and in the oath there is something that indicates a connection to it, like the great distance between the night and the day, and between the male and the female. They are completely different, and likewise they diverge in their outcomes and their means, just as there is a great distance between the success of the one who purifies it and the failure of the one who corrupts it, mentioned in the surah before it.

Then He elaborated this scattering in the detail that follows: ﴿As for him who gives and fears (Allah),﴾ ﴿and affirms the best reward,﴾ ﴿We will ease him toward ease.﴾ ﴿But as for him who is niggardly and considers himself self-sufficient,﴾ ﴿and denies the best reward,﴾ ﴿We will ease him toward hardship.﴾

How far apart are giving, stinginess, affirmation, denial, ease, and hardship! He stated "gives" without qualification so that it would include every kind of giving: of his wealth, his standing, and his effort, even a good word, and even a cheerful face, as in the hadith: "And that you meet your brother with a cheerful face." As for "al-husna" (the best), it was said: it means the recompense for deeds; it was said: it means the replacement for what is spent; it was said: it means "There is no god but Allah"; and it was said: it means Paradise.

What the Qur'an supports is the last of these, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. They said: the "best" is Paradise, and the "more" is looking upon His Noble Face. This meaning encompasses all the other meanings, for it is the best replacement for everything the servant spends, and the best and finest recompense for any deed whatever it may be, and it is not reached except through "There is no god but Allah."

His saying ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾ and His saying ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾ come after mention of "gives and fears" in the first, and "is niggardly and considers himself self-sufficient" in the second.

It was said: this indicates that doing obedience leads to easing toward another obedience, and doing disobedience pushes toward another disobedience.

Ibn Kathir said: like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-An'am: 110].

Then he said: The verses on this meaning are many, indicating that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, rewards whoever intends good with success in it, and whoever intends evil with abandonment, and all of that is by a predetermined decree.

The hadiths indicating this are many. It is mentioned from Abu Bakr in Ahmad, from Ali in al-Bukhari, from Abdullah ibn Umar in Ahmad, and a large number with multiple narrations. The most comprehensive and most authentic of them is the hadith of Ali in al-Bukhari. Ali said: "We were with the Prophet ﷺ in the graveyard of al-Gharqad at a funeral, and he said: 'There is not one of you except that his seat in Paradise or his seat in the Fire has been written.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, should we not rely (on that)?' He said: 'Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for.' Then he recited: ﴿As for him who gives and fears﴾ ﴿and affirms the best reward﴾ ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾ up to His saying ﴿toward hardship.﴾" So these are among the verses connected to the discussion of qadar (divine decree).

This question has been discussed repeatedly before. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Note.

Abu Hayyan said: His saying ﴿We will ease him toward hardship﴾ came by way of contrast, because hardship admits no ease in it. End of quote.

From the standpoint of style this is possible, but it is not far-fetched that the meaning of facilitation is actually present, since what is observed is that among those whom Allah has forsaken, God forbid, there is found acceptance, readiness, and contentment with what is heavier and harder for others, and they see what they are in as easy and facilitated, with no discomfort for them in it, rather they even relish the unlawful and seek its taste.

As one person related to me: a thief had stopped stealing out of shame before people. After his wealth grew and he grew old, he gave a man some dirhams to steal for him from his neighbor's crop. The man went off, circled around from another direction, and brought him a fruit from his own crop, meaning the crop of the thief himself. When he ate it, he spat it out and said: "There is no taste of the stolen in it; where did you get it?" He said: "I got it from your crop." (He said:) "Are you not ashamed before yourself? You steal while you have what suffices you." He was embarrassed and stopped.

It is related from Umar the complete opposite of that: when he asked his servant to give him to drink from the milk in his waterskin, and when he tasted it, he disliked its taste and said to the servant: "Where is this from?" He said: "I passed by the camels of the zakat and they milked some for me, and here it is." So Umar put his finger in his mouth and vomited up what he had drunk.

It is the sensitivity to the unlawful that Umar disliked, and he sensed the unlawful and vomited it up. This and that are by facilitation from Allah, exalted is He. And the Prophet ﷺ spoke truly: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for."

In ordinary affairs we see the people of professions and crafts, each one content with his work and facilitated for it, and so is the whole order of the cosmos. What matters here is that each of obedience and disobedience has its effect upon what follows it.

Note.

It was said: this comparison between ﴿whoever gives and fears﴾ ﴿and affirms the best reward﴾ and ﴿whoever is niggardly and considers himself self-sufficient﴾ ﴿and denies the best reward﴾ was about Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) and others among the polytheists.

It is known that the consideration is with the generality of the wording, so it is general for everyone who ﴿gives and fears﴾ and ﴿affirms﴾, or ﴿is niggardly and considers himself self-sufficient﴾ and ﴿denies﴾. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 92, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls into ruin.﴾

This is a refutation of "whoever is stingy and considers himself self-sufficient." The word "ma" (what/not) here may be a negation particle, meaning: nothing will avail him, as in His saying: ﴿What good has my wealth done me?﴾ [al-Haqqah: 28], and His saying: ﴿The day when neither wealth nor children will avail﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 88].

It may also be an interrogative, and His saying ﴿when he falls into ruin﴾ means: into the Fire, seeking refuge with Allah, or "falls into ruin" in his deeds, so that his end is the Fire because of his stinginess in this world. This is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. They will have the things they withheld hung around their necks on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Al 'Imran: 180], and the rest of the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 92, verse 12:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾

Regarding this, the scholars have several views (awjuh, sing. wajh). Among them: the path of guidance indicates and leads to Us, unlike misguidance.

Among them also: Allah's commitment to the creation that He will give them guidance. This view is open to difficulty, since some of the creation whom Allah has not guided.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, examined this matter in dispelling the appearance of contradiction, namely that the answer to it lies in the fact that guidance is general and specific. And Allah knows best.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-453) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Layl

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾.

It indicates that Allah has committed Himself to guiding the creation, although there are many verses which indicate that He does not guide some people, such as His saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiant people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 108].

And His saying: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 258].

And His saying: ﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved﴾ — the verse [Ali 'Imran: 86] — and other verses besides these.

The answer is what has preceded, that guidance is used in the Qur'an in a specific and a general sense. So the affirmation of the general and the negation of the specific, and the negation of the more specific, does not necessitate the negation of the more general.

As for the view of the one who said that the meaning of the verse is that the path which indicates to Us and to obedience to Us is guidance and not misguidance, and the view of the one who said that the meaning of the verse is that whoever takes the path of guidance reaches Allah, then there is no difficulty in the verse at all.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 92, verse 13:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life.﴾

That is: with complete disposal and command. Allah, the Exalted, has explained this in Surat al-Fatihah: ﴿All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah: 2], meaning the One who disposes of affairs in this world, ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4], meaning the One who alone disposes of affairs in the Hereafter: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

This serves as evidence of His facilitating for His servants what they wish in this world, and of His recompensing them as He wills in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 92, verse 14:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾

That is, that blazes (tatalazzá). Al-Laẓẓá (the blazing flame) is the pure flame. In describing the Fire here as "blazing," although it has many other attributes, among them al-Saʿīr (the Blaze), Saqar, al-Jaḥīm (the Hellfire), al-Hāwiyah (the Abyss), and others,

He mentioned here a specific category, namely those who ﴿denied and turned away﴾ [al-Layl: 16], as was mentioned previously in another place, where it is also described with Laẓá in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No! Indeed, it is Laẓá, a remover of scalps﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 15-16], then He clarified its people by His saying: ﴿Calling to himself those who turned their backs and turned away﴾ ﴿And gathered [wealth] and hoarded﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 17].

It is as here: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾ ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched﴾ ﴿who denied and turned away﴾ [al-Layl: 14-16], and this is the meaning of His saying before it: ﴿But as for one who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾ ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾ [al-Layl: 8-9]. This indicates that the Fire has several states, or zones, or abodes, each abode being specific to a category of people. Laẓá is specific to this category, while Saqar is specific to those who were not among the worshippers and who used to plunge along with the plungers, and the like. Supporting this is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 145]. Just as Paradise has abodes and levels according to the deeds of the believers. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 92, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿None will enter it except the most wretched﴾ ﴿who denied and turned away﴾ ﴿But the most righteous will be spared it﴾ ﴿who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾

This verse is one of the places of apparent difficulty (mawadi' al-iham), and it has not been addressed in resolving the apparent contradiction (iham al-idtirab). It explicitly states, in a restrictive manner ('ala sabil al-hasr), that none will burn in the Fire except the most wretched, while the verse of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is none of you but will pass over it. That is an absolute decree from your Lord﴾ [Maryam: 71] indicates that all will pass over it.

The answer is given in two respects. The first, as al-Zamakhshari said: the verse contrasts the state of a great one among the polytheists with that of a great one among the believers, so that their two contrasting attributes are emphasized.

Thus He said "the most wretched" and made it specific to the burning, as if the Fire had been created only for him; and He said "the most righteous" and made it specific to Paradise, as if Paradise had been created only for him. It has been said concerning the two: they are Abu Jahl or Umayyah ibn Khalaf, the polytheists, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. Abu Hayyan related this from al-Zamakhshari.

The second respect: the "sala" (burning) is entering and remaining, and that the fuel of the Fire be on the basis of eternal abiding. Passing over (wurud) and entering temporarily, limited by a time, is other than "sala," because of His saying in the verse of passing over, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is none of you but will pass over it﴾ [Maryam: 71], ﴿Then We will save those who feared Allah, and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [Maryam: 72]. The difficulty remains concerning those who feared Allah and the most righteous, and it is answered: the righteous one passes over it, while the most righteous does not perceive its passing, like one who passes by it as a flash of lightning. And Allah knows best.

Were it not for the emphasis in the verse of passing over, by the coming of the particle "min" and "illa," and His saying: ﴿That is an absolute decree from your Lord﴾, were it not for these mentioned features, it would be possible to say that it is specific to this verse, and that the most righteous does not pass over it. However, the presence of those mentioned features prevents saying that it is specific. And Allah knows best.

In it is an affirmation of the destiny of the two categories mentioned earlier: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾ ﴿and believes in the best reward﴾, and ﴿As for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾ ﴿and denies the best reward﴾. The burning of the former is due to denial, turning away and aversion, which is the very essence of wretchedness, while the most righteous, who affirmed the truth, is spared it. The outcome of his affirmation is that he gives his wealth to purify himself, and he made the giving of wealth as a result of affirmation a matter of utmost importance.

That is because the servant does not give any of his wealth except in exchange; for the whole world is based on exchange, even animals: you give them fodder and they give you what corresponds to it of service or milk. Etc.

So the believer who affirms the good reward gives, and awaits the fuller recompense: a good deed for ten like it, because he believes that he is dealing with Allah, as in His saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245].

As for the denier, he did not believe in a deferred recompense, so he gives nothing, because he finds no immediate return, and does not expect a deferred reward. For this reason, those who had settled in the abode and faith loved those who emigrated to them, and shared with them, and did not find in their breasts any need for what they had been given, and preferred them over themselves even though they themselves were in need, out of faith in what is with Allah. Whereas the hypocrites would spend only unwillingly and would only bring out the inferior, which they would not have accepted from others except by overlooking its defects. All of this is caused by affirming or denying the good reward.

For this reason, there came in the authentic hadith: "Charity is a proof," meaning: a proof of the soundness of faith in what Allah has promised the righteous, of multiplied good replacement.

His saying: ﴿who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾ means: he purifies himself and seeks increase, since tazkiyah comes in the sense of growth, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 103]. This is a response to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself﴾ [al-A'la: 14], and to the general sense of: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah﴾ [al-Layl: 5]. It cannot be said that it refers to zakat on wealth, because zakat was not legislated except in Medina, and the surah is Meccan according to the majority; it has been said to be Medinan, but the correct view is the first.

Note.

It has also been said that what is meant by His saying: ﴿But the most righteous will be spared it﴾ ﴿who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾, to the end of the surah, was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, because he used to free the weak Muslims and those who were tortured for their Islam in Mecca. It was said to him: "If only you bought the strong ones who would support you and defend you." So Allah revealed the verses up to His saying: ﴿And no one has a favour with him that is repaid﴾ ﴿except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-Layl: 19-20]. The seeking of the countenance of the Lord is itself, and affirming the good reward, that is, for the sake of Allah's countenance, hoping for reward from Allah.

As mentioned before, the lesson is in the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion, and the form of the occasion is certainly included. So this is a great glad tiding for the Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: ﴿And he will surely be satisfied﴾, with the utmost emphasis from Allah, the Exalted, on His promise to him, (ﷺ) and may He be pleased with him.

Ibn Kathir mentioned that in the Two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever spends a pair in the way of Allah, the keepers of Paradise will call him: O servant of Allah, this is good. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, there is no harm for whoever is called from it; but is anyone called from all of them? He said: Yes, and I hope you will be among them." End quote.

And indeed we hope from Allah the same, as a bounty from Him, exalted is He.

Note.

Regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he will surely be satisfied﴾ [al-Layl: 21]. Ibn Kathir mentioned the consensus of the exegetes that it refers to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, as the highest station of glad tidings; because this very description was addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ) definitively in the following surah, Surat al-Duha: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 4-5]. So it is a promise shared by the Siddiq and the Messenger (ﷺ), except that in the case of the Messenger (ﷺ) the giving is attributed to Allah, the Exalted, with the attribute of Lordship: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you﴾, just as the giving is mentioned in it, which indicates other than him (ﷺ). This is known necessarily, that he (ﷺ) has gifts which no one else shares with him, as will come, Allah willing.
